previous_description: A granular access grant specifying which operations a named actor may perform on an InformationEntity, subject to a qualifying constraint expression. Implements attribute-based access control (ABAC) at the information asset level, per NIST SP 800-162 (ABAC Guide) and NIST SP 800-53 AC-3(14).
definition: An access grant that authorizes one specific actor to perform a listed set of operations on a single InformationEntity. The grant applies only while an attribute-based constraint expression evaluates to true at decision time. It differs from a role-assigned Permission because it names the grantee directly and carries its own qualifying condition.

distinguish_from.when: the grant is a reusable resource+action entitlement assigned to Roles rather than to a named actor, and has no per-grant constraint expression
authority is transferred from one actor (delegator) to another (delegatee), possibly time-bounded, rather than granted directly on an information asset
access is gated by the actor declaring a purpose or justification rather than by an attribute-based boolean constraint
the element is only the field/operator/value predicate itself, not the grant binding an actor and operations to an information asset

standard_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 AC-3(13) Attribute-Based Access Control; NIST SP 800-162 ABAC policy; STS-ml authorisation
code_evidence: An ABAC policy line naming a concrete subject, data asset, actions and condition, e.g. Casbin `p, billing-svc, customer_pii, read, r.sub.region == r.obj.region`
A cloud IAM or KMS policy statement whose Principal is a specific user or service, whose Resource is a named data store or dataset, and which has an Action list and a Condition block
An OPA/Rego or Cedar `permit` rule keyed on a specific principal id and data category, with a `when`/`if` clause comparing subject attributes to resource attributes
notes: AC-3(14) is 'Individual Access' in Rev.5; ABAC is AC-3(13), so the definition should be corrected. The operations array has no enum; reuse the ResourceOperation enum. The accesses and governs edges to informationentity, plus the reverse governs edge, are redundant. The actor and constraint strings duplicate the assigned-to and constrained-by relationships.
